svg.title: TOPAK H5 — How a proof is built and kept in step
svg.desc: Twenty-two of the twenty-seven modules under spec/ have a proof module (ADR-0046, Batch 25; G10 §2.9), and spec/proof-sync.sh records why each of the other five has none. This diagram is the mechanism, not the inventory: one proof module part by part, the four shapes its inductive invariants took and what the proofs of 2026.10.04 and 10.05 added, and the loop that keeps each proof the proof of its specification, now with a certified run beside it (ADR-0046 A1, Batch 28). TLC checks the mutations and witnesses, which are existential claims; the prover proves the invariants, which are universal, under named hypotheses (ADR-0046 §1); a proof is certified when every obligation is closed by the prover's normalization, a checked proof, or LS4. None is a claim about the running reference (T-0045-28). Which modules are proved, with their counts, is H3; certification route by route is H6; each property's hypotheses are G3's "Breaks under" column. Section 4 sets beside the loop the same loop for a Lean re-encoding (ADR-0053, ratified in Batch 36; H7), which proves the same theorems again, of an encoding, and is kept in step the same way.
svg.text: TOPAK · H5

text.tspan: How a proof is built and kept in step

svg.text: Twenty-two of the twenty-seven modules under spec/ have a proof module (ADR-0046, Batch 25; G10 §2.9), and spec/proof-sync.sh records why each of the other five has none. This diagram is the mechanism, not the inventory: one proof module part by part, the four shapes its inductive invariants took and what the proofs of 2026.10.04 and 10.05 added, and the loop that keeps each proof the proof of its specification, now with

a certified run beside it (ADR-0046 A1, Batch 28). TLC checks the mutations and witnesses, which are existential claims; the prover proves the invariants, which are universal, under named hypotheses (ADR-0046 §1); a proof is certified when every obligation is closed by the prover's normalization, a checked proof, or LS4. None is a claim about the running reference (T-0045-28). Which modules are proved, with their counts, is H3;

certification route by route is H6; each property's hypotheses are G3's "Breaks under" column. Section 4 sets beside the loop the same loop for a Lean re-encoding (ADR-0053, ratified in Batch 36; H7), which proves the same theorems again, of an encoding, and is kept in step the same way.

text.tspan: 1 · One proof module, part by part:
1 · Extend the frozen module; never edit it

svg.text: EXTENDS Lease_A1, TLAPS. Lease_A1.tla (0b5eac7a7309be2f) is frozen by the records that cite it; the
proof restates nothing from it (ADR-0046 §4).
A constant a run script set per row becomes a named ASSUME where a proof needs it: Active \subseteq
AllEntries in Anchor, Declared \in 0..3 in Confinement, Filtered \in BOOLEAN in RunConfinement
(FilteredBool). Lease_A1 needs none: MaxEpoch and MaxFence only cut the state space, so its theorems
hold for every value.
An unnamed ASSUME in a base module is a fact to TLC and nothing to the prover; it is restated as a lemma
proved from the definitions (GenesisEntries in Anchor_proof).

text.tspan: 2 · A type invariant, proved under every mutation

svg.text: TypeOK: lease and prev in [Principals -> LeaseRec], epoch and fence naturals, revoked \subseteq
Principals.
InitTypeOK and NextTypeOK, one step per action, with no hypothesis on Mut.
Its job: an EXCEPT on one principal leaves the others alone, which the prover cannot see unless the function's
domain is in scope (proof-method §3, §4).

text.tspan: 3 · One inductive step per invariant, under its hypothesis

svg.text: Each theorem takes as hypothesis only the mutations that break it, e.g. ASSUME Mut # "M_FENCE". The
hypotheses restate the binding table's "Breaks under" column (ADR-0046 §4, §5).
The Next lemma has one step per action: UNCHANGED vars, Revoke, Grant(p), Renew(p), Act(p),
EndRound(p), RevokeLease(p). A failed step names the action.
The inductive invariant is the property alone, the property with TypeOK, or more (section 2).
Init => Inv and Inv /\ [Next]_vars => Inv', then PTL DEF Spec: three lines per theorem.
SafeAlways under Mut = "none" cites one Spec => []P step per theorem before its PTL step: the prover
cannot discharge a theorem's hypothesis inside PTL (proof-method §4).
A property true in every state needs no induction: Rung0NeverContained is a state lemma, Rung0Valid,
lifted by PTL.
Mut # "M_RENEW", Mut # "M_ROLE", Mut # "M_LOWER"
TypeOK and the property
RenewRefines: under the hypothesis a renewal refines its predecessor; NextMonotone: seven cases
A relation between lease and prev, kept per principal
The property alone
NextFenced: the work is in Act, whose epoch check makes both epochs equal
A flag (staleAdmitted) and an append-only set (acted)
None: true in every state
Rung0Valid, by the definition of Contained; then PTL
A valid state predicate
TypeOK and the property
NextRevoked: the grant guard refuses a revoked principal; a renewal needs a live lease
A set the property quantifies over
One Spec => []P step per theorem, then PTL DEF Safe
The conjunction

text.tspan: 5 · One lemma per mutation, saying what it admits

svg.text: MutRenewAllowsAll, MutRoleIgnored, MutLowerAccepted: under each, RenewalAllowed admits a renewal that does not refine its predecessor.
MutFenceIgnoresEpoch: EpochOK(p) holds at any epoch. MutRungContainsAll: every live lease is Contained, rung 0 included.
MutRevokeGrantsAgain: ENABLED Grant(p) for a revoked principal with no live lease and fence room, proved BY ExpandENABLED.
Each names the guard the mutation removes, which is the guard the theorem's hypothesis keeps. The counterexample itself stays TLC's: that a mutation reaches a bad state is existential (ADR-0046 §2).

text.tspan: 6 · Checked by the prover, measured by digest
Accepted · T-0045-31 · ADR-0046 B25, A1 B28

svg.text: tools/tlapm --cleanfp --strict Lease_A1_proof.tla: --cleanfp takes nothing from an earlier run; --strict makes a failed obligation a non-zero exit.
proof-results.sh prints the results file: the Modules: line with Lease_A1.tla (0b5eac7a7309be2f) and Lease_A1_proof.tla (6f39c7711252c8de), the prover binary (e150fb793fb28592, T-0045-31), the
assumptions, theorems and lemmas, and "All 200 obligations proved". The file is d4b39bd7094c38d1.
Then certified (ADR-0046 A1): proof-cert.sh Lease_A1_proof reruns it with cvc5 behind smt-checked in place of Z3 and Isabelle checking Zenon. Lease_A1-proof-cert-results-2026.10.04.txt (
a9e59ca0937e3fed): 121 trivial, 73 SMT with a proof ethos accepted, 0 Zenon, 1 Isabelle, 5 LS4. Certified: 195 rest on normalization or a checked proof, 5 on LS4 (H6).
A proof of the module, not of the reference's grant path (T-0045-28).

text.tspan: 2 · The four shapes the inductive invariants took

svg.text: The modules were written for mutation testing, so each property was instrumented for TLC to flip, and that made it local to the guard a mutation removes: the "Breaks under" column was in effect a list of which guard each proof would rest on (proof-method §5). Two forms needed no inductive invariant of their own: a predicate true in every state (Rung0NeverContained), and a property set once at a commit action and frozen after it (RulesFloorNV_rev5, at
Promote).

text.tspan: A flag set at the violating action

svg.text: DenyByAnyOf == ~admittedOverFinding. Admit(t), guarded by ~Blocked(t), sets
admittedOverFinding' = admittedOverFinding \/ (Found(t) \cap W(t) # {}).
Inductive by itself. Under the hypothesis the condition is false at the one action that can set the flag: a
propositional check against that action's guard.
Where: FloorRouting, FloorComposition's four flags, Observers, the coupling flags in Coupling and
RunCoupling, Lease_A1's staleAdmitted.

text.tspan: An append-only set, and what may be appended

svg.text: acted' = acted \cup {[act |-> a, kind |-> KindOf[s]]}, with the auxiliary Alphabets == \A s \in
Seats : lease[s].live => lease[s].alphabet = KindBound(KindOf[s]).
One state fact about what the appending action can append: the guard's precondition, written as an
invariant.
Where: Seats and RunSeats (the alphabet), BreakGlass (bgDid; the floor holds of the issued rules),
NonComposition (created and retained; the records NC1 needs were created, and only admitted effects
went via break-glass). RunConfinement's effects needs no auxiliary: both invariants are inductive on their
own (116 obligations).

text.tspan: Generation binding: the one that was invented

svg.text: ContainedMeansConfined: the record Act appends depends on state set three actions earlier, at launch,
appraisal and grant.
Six clauses with TypeOK: GuestImg (the running image is the booted one), GuestGen (a live guest carries the
current generation), LowRungHonest (below rung 2 the booted image is the asked one), PendingBinds and
LeaseBinds (an attested appraisal and a lease above rung 0 remember a generation, and while that guest
stands its asked image is the profile and was booted), and the property.
Preserved because a relaunch strictly raises the generation, and Act admits only against the lease's, the
check M_UNBOUND removes. 502 obligations, every rung at once; the successor Confinement_A1_proof, 503,
changes one case split to Declared <= 1: rung 0 joins rung 1 under LowRungHonest.
UnreadBounded: what the Observer has not read stays within K.
Shape holds under every mutation: Future (later rounds are zero), MarkLeSeq (the mark is at most the
sequence), SealedIdle (an idle round's seal is its sequence). On it, the two layers the coupling needs: Past
(earlier marks equal their seals) and Bound (seq - mark[round] <= K).
Each clause answers what one action needs to keep the bound. RunCoupling adds SeqIsEff and
PastSeal. Holds for every K, R and MaxRound: K < R is not a premise (ADR-0046 §5).

text.tspan: What the seven proofs written since G9 added to the four shapes

svg.text: Emergency, Labels, ToolList, Operators and Correlator on 2026.10.04; the successors BreakGlass_A1 and NonComposition_A1 on 2026.10.05; each is proved and certified (G10 §3). The method did not change; these are the habits proof-method.md §1 and ToO §11.3 record.

text.tspan: One lemma on the shapes a step can have

svg.text: Labels_proof (651 obligations, ten invariants): one lemma on the three shapes a step has, with Actuate's
LET named part by part; then "labels cover the truth", from which the floor's minimum follows by the forbid that
would have fired.
All 216 of its SMT obligations certified at the default timeout (proof-certification.md §10).
Labels needed that only an item that exists is in the guest; Emergency that every lease's holder is a person,
not only the emergency seat's (ToO §11.3).
Operators and Emergency state the lease properties over every lease, not only live ones: "every granted
lease has a quorum at its root", "no lease is wider than its seating", since a regrant revives a lease the stated
property is silent about (proof-method.md §1).
Operators' DenyAlwaysAvailable and Correlator's LagNeverGates are state lemmas, as RunCoupling's
ConsultNeverCoupled was.
An ENABLED goal may go to Zenon, whose script then has to reconstruct in Isabelle to certify.
Operators_proof has two that Isabelle accepted; Emergency_proof had one, in a lemma no theorem used,
that it could not check, and the lemma was removed and its fact left to a TLC witness.

text.tspan: A successor can drop an assumption

svg.text: BreakGlass_proof assumes "R7" \in Active. BreakGlass_A1_proof (45 obligations) does not: under the
kind's alphabet as decided R7 has nothing to refuse (ADR-0026 A2), so it takes R7 only as a hypothesis under
one mutation, Mut = "M_KIND" => "R7" \in Active, beside Mut # "M_SCOPE".
NonComposition_A1_proof (96) proves NC1 and NC2 with none of its three mutations on, since each breaks
both; the third, M3, is new with the seating: an activation's record kept only while its round is live.

text.tspan: 3 · The loop that keeps a proof the proof of its specification

svg.text: A proof module extends the module it proves, so the two can drift in exactly one way: the base module changes. The binding is the Modules: line of the results file; the repair is the successor discipline the corpus already has for modules (proof-method §6).
Lease_A1.tla, cited by ADR-0031. A change is a successor
module, never an edit.
Lease_A1_proof.tla: EXTENDS Lease_A1, TLAPS, with the
hypotheses the base module must not carry.
tools/tlapm --cleanfp --strict; binary
e150fb793fb28592, not tracked, named in the corpus since
2026.10.03 by tools/TLAPS-PIN (version, commit 7824dab,
the digest's first sixteen hex, backends). The wrapper refuses
another binary unless TLAPM_UNPINNED=1; proof-sync.sh
reports a results file citing another prover. G10 item 73:
discharged; the full digest is still owed.
proof-results.sh: Modules: names the digest of every
module in the EXTENDS chain as proved, then the prover's
digest and "All N obligations proved".
proof-cert.sh <M>_proof reruns the same proof with Z3
replaced by cvc5 behind smt-checked and Zenon checked by
Isabelle, and prints <M>-proof-cert-results-<date>.txt:
every obligation by route, and "All N obligations proved…" or
NOT CERTIFIED: <reason>.
Run proof-results.sh first: faster, and it finds real failures
(proof-certification.md §10). G10 §5: a proof is certified or its
results file says why not. Route by route: H6.
ADR-0046 §4 cites base, proof and results digests, frozen from
Batch 25; A1 cites the certified results files (B28). G9's two are
frozen from G9, and the six new modules of G10, their proofs
and results files from G10 (G10 §3).
EXTENDS
checked
printed
rerun
cited
For each <M>_proof.tla, the newest results file's digests against the tree: IN SYNC, or STALE naming the module that moved, or MISSING
RESULTS; and every results file's prover against tools/TLAPS-PIN.
Then every base module without a proof, with the reason recorded: Mechanism (a trace replay), ConfinementRefinement (predicates over replayed
trace states), Lease and RulesFloorNV (superseded), RulesFloorBase (definitions). Exits 1 on a stale proof, a missing results file, a prover other
than the pin's, or a proofless module with no reason.

text.tspan: : did the drift break the proof?

svg.text: Re-checks each stale proof. A changed guard fails at its
action's step, a changed property at Init or Next, a changed
mutation at a hypothesis that no longer discharges.
Write the successor module, suffix _A1, its predecessor cited by digest and not edited (G10 §5): Lease to Lease_A1, Confinement to
Confinement_A1, and since 2026.10.05 BreakGlass and NonComposition to BreakGlass_A1 and NonComposition_A1, where the predecessors
model X1 (ADR-0052 R5). Copy the proof to <Successor>_proof.tla, point its EXTENDS at the successor, and re-prove.
Generate its results file with proof-results.sh, then its certified run; commit them with the successor and its TLC results. The record that cites the
successor cites its proof by digest; the frozen pair stays as it was.
Confinement_A1's proof needed one case split changed, Declared = 1 to Declared <= 1, not unchanged as the drafter first wrote (G9 §3, finding
It reads the -proof-results- files only. A certified results file
binds itself to its modules the same way, by its Modules: line,
and nothing compares that line with the tree.
Nothing here reports a change to the wrapper, the solver or the
checker: their digests are in each certified file's header, and a
rerun that differs is a different certification
(proof-certification.md §5).
its digests
STALE
repair
new digest
successor proof
Copy the proof module to scratch, flip one hypothesis to the mutation it excludes, and run the prover. It must reject the proof, at the guard the
Anchor_proof with Mut = "M_FLOOR": 1 of 40 obligations fails, at Floor(r) in the Issue case (ADR-0046 B25). A proof that survives the flip is proving
the wrong thing.
A mutated proof is not an artefact: it leaves no file (G8 §5).

text.tspan: Why the proofs are not merged into the modules

svg.text: A base module is frozen by digest; adding a proof would make it a successor of itself.
TLC runs the base module through tools/tla2tools.jar without the prover's library; a merged module would carry EXTENDS TLAPS into every TLC
run.
The proof carries hypotheses (Mut # "M_X", "R7" \in Active) that the module must not: the module is written so TLC can flip each mutation. Each
reason is sufficient (proof-method §6).

text.tspan: A live module in the chain:

svg.text: Anchor, BreakGlass and now BreakGlass_A1 extend it. It is the live definition of the floor by its own header; ADR-0046 §4 called it frozen, and erratum
E1 (Batch 26) corrected that.
The results files record the digest proved (cf2351de2b39cccf, unchanged at G10), so a change shows as STALE for each proof whose Modules: line
names it, and each needs a successor proof.
It is behind the records: it still carries bgScope and R6's bound of two, where ADR-0026 A2 (provisional, Batch 34) makes the count one (G10 §2.1;
item 90).

text.tspan: 4 · The same loop, for a Lean re-encoding (ADR-0053, B36)

svg.text: A re-encoding does not extend its module: it is a second statement of it, in Lean, beside it under spec/lean/, and the base module does not know it exists. So it drifts the way a proof does, when the base module changes, and one more way a proof cannot: the Lean can say something other than the module, which is read and not checked. Every row below is the TLAPS loop's, matched (proof-method §5b, §6).
EXTENDS it: the proof is of the frozen text itself
Restates it beside the text: the theorems are of the encoding, read against the module

text.tspan: What binds the result to the text

svg.text: The Modules: line: every module of the EXTENDS chain by digest
The Transcribes: line: every TLA+ module encoded, by repository path and digest; the Sources: line: every Lean file
spec/lean/results.sh, through tools/lean-report.sh: a clean build, #print axioms sorted, and the replay
"All N obligations proved" (T-0045-31)
"Build completed" and leanchecker --fresh: every constant replayed through the kernel in a fresh environment (T-0045-37, proposed)
spec/proof-sync.sh: IN SYNC, STALE, MISSING RESULTS
tools/lean-sync.sh: the same three, for spec/lean, mechanism/lean and floor/lean
tools/TLAPS-PIN; tools/tlapm refuses another binary
tools/LEAN-PIN; lean-sync.sh refuses a results file naming another kernel
tools/install-tlaps.sh, 1.9 GB, not tracked
tools/install-lean.sh through elan, about 2 GB, not tracked
A successor module and a successor proof; the frozen pair stays
A successor encoding, a new Lean file; the old one stays as the encoding of the frozen module
Cited by digest in a ratified record (ADR-0046 §4)
With its base module, on ADR-0053's ratification; until then cited by none
Flip one hypothesis in a scratch copy: the prover must reject the proof at the guard
Mutate one definition in a scratch copy: the build must fail in the theorem the mutation breaks (eighteen for spec/lean, 2026.10.05)
The certified results file's Modules: line
Whether the encoding says what the module says: that is the reading
They fail in different places. The TLAPS proof trusts LS4 for the temporal step and the prover's front end; the Lean proof trusts the encoding. A theorem
proved by both is wrong only if both fail.
The Lean proof is not a successor of the TLAPS proof, and neither replaces the other: the TLA+ module, its proof and its certified run stay canonical
The same strengthenings carried over. Every Lean proof reuses the inductive invariant its TLAPS proof found, which is why thirteen modules took a day;
what TLAPS proves as TypeOK, Lean's types carry.
One more drift than a proof has: an encoding can be wrong where a proof extending the text cannot. The header of each Lean file names where a
reading was chosen.
